config.title: Lifting State Up

intro.title: Lifting State Up
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple temperature converter app that allows you to switch between Celsius and Fahrenheit inputs. You will learn the concept of 'lifting state up,' which means moving shared state to the closest common parent component to keep your data synchronized. The main technologies involved are Vue components, reactive state with the ref function, and event handling with custom events. This approach helps you manage data flow in a predictable way, making your Vue applications easier to maintain and debug.
intro.usecase: Lifting state up is essential in Vue applications where multiple components need to share and synchronize data. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, product filters in a sidebar component must update the product list in the main content area. Similarly, in a multi-step form, user input from different form sections needs to be collected and validated in a parent component. This pattern ensures consistent data flow across interactive UI elements like settings panels, real-time collaboration tools, or dashboard widgets that display synchronized information.

objectives: Initialize reactive state in a parent component to manage shared data.
Bind reactive state from a parent component to child components using props.
Implement custom event handlers in child components to emit changes.
Update parent state by handling custom events emitted from child components.
Control the flow of data by lifting state to the nearest common ancestor.
Render dynamic UI elements that reflect synchronized state across multiple components.
Manipulate the application structure to centralize state management for sibling components.

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and ref from the Vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue APIs for reactive state management.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and ref APIs are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the parent component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ParentComponent with a template section that returns a single root element.
steps.hint: Define a component using Vue's defineComponent or a simple object with a template property.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create the parent component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ParentComponent is defined with a template that returns a single root element.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is defined and exports a template with a single root element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named ParentComponent and has a template with a single root element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it ParentComponent and included a template with a single root element.

steps.title: Initialize shared state in parent
steps.instruction: Inside the parent component's setup function, use ref to create a reactive count variable initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Remember to call ref(0) to create a reactive reference with an initial value of 0.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state in Vue
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component now has a reactive count variable that can be shared with child components.
successCriteria: A count variable is declared using ref(0) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref(0) to initialize the count variable inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the setup function, declare a count variable using ref(0) to create reactive state.

steps.title: Create the first child component
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named ChildComponent that defines props to receive data from the parent.
steps.hint: Define a new component object with a props property that accepts data from the parent component.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent component is defined with a props property to receive data from the parent.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined as a Vue component with a props property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ChildComponent is properly defined as a Vue component with a props property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to define ChildComponent as a Vue component with props.

steps.title: Create the second child component
steps.instruction: Create a second Vue component named AnotherChildComponent with a props definition.
steps.hint: Define a new component object with a props property, similar to how you created the first child component.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a second child component defined with props, ready to receive data from the parent.
successCriteria: AnotherChildComponent is defined as a Vue component object with a props property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it has a props definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second child component isn't properly defined yet. Create a Vue component named AnotherChildComponent with props.

steps.title: Define decrement handler in parent
steps.instruction: In the parent component's setup function, define a function named decrement that decreases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that modifies the shared state. Use count.value to access and update the reactive value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will have a decrement function that modifies the shared count state.
successCriteria: A decrement function is defined in the parent component's setup that decreases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your decrement function properly decreases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement handler is not defined correctly. It should be a function that decreases count.value by 1.

steps.title: Add child components to parent template
steps.instruction: In the parent component's template, add both ChildComponent and AnotherChildComponent, passing the count state as a prop named 'count' to each.
steps.hint: Use the component names as custom HTML tags in the template. Pass the count ref's value as a prop using v-bind or the colon shorthand.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component's template now includes both child components, each receiving the count state as a prop.
successCriteria: ChildComponent and AnotherChildComponent are both present in the template, each with a prop named 'count' bound to the count ref.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added at least one child component, but make sure to include both ChildComponent and AnotherChildComponent, each with the count prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet include both child components with the count prop. Remember to use the component names as custom tags and bind count to a prop.

steps.title: Add buttons to parent template
steps.instruction: In the parent component's template, add two buttons: one with text 'Increment' and one with text 'Decrement'. Wire each button's click event to the corresponding handler (increment and decrement) that you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind click events to your handler functions. Make sure to call the handlers correctly without parentheses in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component's template will have two buttons that can trigger the increment and decrement handlers when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons with text 'Increment' and 'Decrement' are added to the parent template, each with @click directives calling the correct handler functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the buttons, but the click handlers might not be correctly wired. Make sure each button uses @click with the correct handler name (increment or decrement).
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not properly configured. Add two buttons with text 'Increment' and 'Decrement' and wire their click events to the corresponding handlers.

steps.expectedOutcome: The first child component will show the count value passed from the parent.
successCriteria: First child component template contains a paragraph element
Paragraph displays the count prop using {{ count }}
